posts.title: Plum cake that uses a whole kilo
posts.excerpt: A kilo of węgierki in one tin. Oil, oat milk, no eggs, 1 hour.
posts.content:
Every September my neighbour Pani Halina leaves a bag of węgierki on my door handle. Every September I make this.

It's the simplest cake I know. The plums sink a little and go jammy at the bottom. That's correct.

Serves

12 pieces

Prep

15 min

Cook

50 min

Good to know

Better on day two

Jump to the recipe

Ingredients

For the batter
  • 200g plain flour (or spelt)
  • 100g sugar
  • 2 tsp baking powder
  • A pinch of cinnamon
  • 120ml sunflower oil
  • 200ml oat milk
For the top
  • 1kg plums, halved and stoned
  • 2 tbsp sugar
  • A handful of flaked almonds

Method

1

Heat the oven to 180°C. Oil a 24 × 30 cm tin and line the bottom with paper, because plum juice glues everything.

2

Whisk the dry things, then stir in the oil and oat milk until there are no dry bits. It will be thick, like porridge you forgot about.

3

Spread it in the tin, push the plums in skin side down, close together, and scatter the sugar and almonds over.

4

Bake for 50 minutes, until the edges are brown and the plums have slumped. Cool in the tin.

it works with frozen plums too

Notes from my kitchen

  • Węgierki are drier than big plums. With juicy plums, add 2 tbsp flour to the batter.
  • Spelt flour makes it denser and nuttier. I prefer it now.

Swaps that work

  • Frozen plums: straight from the freezer, 10 minutes longer.
  • Apples in October: thin slices, and more cinnamon.

Keeping it

  • Room temperature: 3 days under a tea towel.
  • Freezer: in pieces, 2 months.

posts.title: Grandma Zosia's barszcz, with one change
posts.excerpt: Clear beetroot soup with sauerkraut brine in place of the starter. Makes 2 litres.
posts.content:
Babcia Zosia made barszcz with a sour starter she kept going for weeks. I don't have the patience, so I use the brine from a jar of sauerkraut. She would say that's cheating. It is.

Serve it clear in a cup, or with cashew cream swirled in, like in the photo.

Serves

Makes 2 litres

Prep

20 min

Cook

50 min

Good to know

Better on day three

Jump to the recipe

Ingredients

For the broth
  • 1kg beetroot, peeled and sliced
  • 1 carrot, 1 parsley root
  • 4 dried porcini
  • 2 bay leaves, 4 allspice berries
To finish
  • 200ml sauerkraut brine
  • 2 garlic cloves, crushed
  • Salt, sugar, marjoram

Method

1

Soak the porcini in a cup of hot water for 20 minutes.

2

Simmer the beetroot, roots, bay and allspice in 2 litres of water for 40 minutes. Don't let it boil hard or it goes brown.

3

Strain, add the mushroom water, the brine and the garlic. Season until it's sour, sweet and salty all at once.

keeps a week, and tastes best on day three

Notes from my kitchen

  • Taste after every addition. The balance is the whole recipe.
  • Keep the cooked beetroot for a salad with horseradish.

Swaps that work

  • No brine: juice of 1 lemon and 2 tbsp cider vinegar.
  • No porcini: 1 tbsp brown miso.

Keeping it

  • Fridge: a week in a jar.
  • Freezer: 3 months, but don't freeze it with the cream in.

posts.title: Pierogi with buckwheat and mushrooms
posts.excerpt: Egg-free dough, a kasza and mushroom filling, about 50 pierogi.
posts.content:
The dough has no egg and nobody at my workshops has ever noticed. The trick is hot water and a rest.

The filling is kasza, fried onion and whatever mushrooms you found. Dried porcini make it taste like Christmas.

Serves

Makes 50

Prep

1 hr

Cook

30 min

Good to know

Freezes well

Jump to the recipe

Ingredients

For the dough
  • 500g plain flour
  • 250ml just-boiled water
  • 3 tbsp oil
  • A pinch of salt
For the filling
  • 150g roasted buckwheat
  • 300g mushrooms
  • 2 onions
  • Salt, pepper, marjoram
To serve
  • 1 onion, fried dark
  • Dill

Method

1

Mix the flour, hot water, oil and salt. Knead for 5 minutes and rest it under a bowl for 30.

2

Cook the buckwheat. Fry the onions and mushrooms until dark, then chop everything together and season hard.

3

Roll thin, cut circles, fill and pinch shut. Boil in batches until they float, then 1 minute more.

4

Serve with the fried onion and a lot of dill.

they freeze well, on a tray first

Notes from my kitchen

  • Season the filling more than you think. The dough is plain.
  • A glass is fine for cutting circles. Mine is 8 cm.

Swaps that work

  • Pearl barley for buckwheat.
  • Smoked tofu, crumbled, instead of half the mushrooms.

Keeping it

  • Freeze on a tray, then in a bag. 3 months.
  • Cook from frozen, 2 minutes longer.

posts.title: Dill pickles in a 3-litre jar
posts.excerpt: Salt-brine ogórki kiszone. No vinegar, a week on the counter.
posts.content:
Ogórki kiszone, the salt-brine kind. No vinegar. They're sour because of time and nothing else.

Use small, firm cucumbers from the market in August, the ones with bumps. Big smooth ones go hollow.

Serves

One 3-litre jar

Prep

20 min

Cook

7 days

Good to know

Lasts until spring

Jump to the recipe

Ingredients

In the jar
  • 2kg small pickling cucumbers
  • 1 big bunch of dill with flowers
  • 6 garlic cloves
  • 2 horseradish leaves or a piece of root
For the brine
  • 2 litres water
  • 60g salt (not iodised)

Method

1

Wash the cucumbers in cold water. Pack them upright into the jar with the dill, garlic and horseradish.

2

Dissolve the salt in the water and pour over until everything is covered. Weigh down with a small plate.

3

Leave on the counter for 3 days, then somewhere cool. Ready in a week.

drink the brine, it's good for you

Notes from my kitchen

  • Cloudy brine is normal. White film on top: skim it off.
  • Horseradish leaves keep them crunchy. Oak or cherry leaves work too.

Swaps that work

  • No horseradish: 2 bay leaves.

Keeping it

  • Cellar or fridge: until spring.
  • Once opened: fridge, 2 weeks.

posts.title: Braised cabbage with smoked tofu and apple
posts.excerpt: Bigos without the three days. One pan, 50 minutes.
posts.content:
A winter pan of food that tastes of bigos without the three days.

Savoy or white cabbage, both fine. The apple goes soft and disappears, which is the point.

Serves

4

Prep

10 min

Cook

40 min

Good to know

Better next day

Jump to the recipe

Ingredients

Vegetables
  • 1 small cabbage, shredded
  • 2 apples, grated
  • 1 onion
Everything else
  • 200g smoked tofu, cubed
  • 2 tbsp tomato paste
  • 1 tsp caraway, 2 bay leaves

Method

1

Fry the onion and tofu until brown.

2

Add the cabbage, apple, paste, caraway, bay and a cup of water. Cover.

3

Cook gently for 40 minutes, stirring now and then. Season with salt and a lot of pepper.

eat it with potatoes and a pickle

Notes from my kitchen

  • Add a handful of sauerkraut at the end for the full bigos taste.

Swaps that work

  • Smoked tofu: 150g fried mushrooms and 1 tsp smoked paprika.

Keeping it

  • Fridge: 4 days.
  • Freezer: 3 months.

posts.title: Broad beans with dill butter
posts.excerpt: July bób from a paper cone, on a plate. 10 minutes.
posts.content:
Bób from a paper cone at the market in July, eaten warm, squeezed out of their skins. This is the same thing on a plate.

Serves

2 as a snack

Prep

2 min

Cook

5 min

Jump to the recipe

Ingredients

You need
  • 500g broad beans in their skins
  • 2 tbsp plant butter
  • A big handful of dill
  • Flaky salt

Method

1

Boil the beans in salted water for 4 minutes and drain.

2

Toss with the butter, chopped dill and salt.

3

Eat with your hands. Pop them out of the skins as you go.

only in July

Notes from my kitchen

  • Only in July. Frozen broad beans are fine in a stew but not here.

Swaps that work

  • Good olive oil instead of butter.

Keeping it

  • Eat them now.

posts.title: Rhubarb compote for May
posts.excerpt: The first kompot of the year. 3 litres, 10 minutes of cooking.
posts.content:
Kompot is the drink of every Polish summer lunch: fruit, water, sugar, cooled. Rhubarb is the first one of the year.

Serves

3 litres

Prep

5 min

Cook

10 min

Good to know

Serve cold

Jump to the recipe

Ingredients

You need
  • 600g rhubarb, chopped
  • 3 litres water
  • 120g sugar
  • 1 strip of lemon peel

Method

1

Bring the water to the boil with the sugar and peel.

2

Add the rhubarb and simmer for 5 minutes, no longer.

3

Cool completely and serve cold with the fruit in.

make a big pot, it goes fast

Notes from my kitchen

  • Strawberries go in from June.

Swaps that work

  • Honey is not vegan, so I use sugar. Maple syrup works.

Keeping it

  • Fridge: 4 days in a big jar.

posts.title: Chanterelles on toast
posts.excerpt: Brushed, fried dry, then onion and dill on rye. 15 minutes.
posts.content:
Cleaned with a brush, not washed. Fried hot and dry first so they squeak, and only then the oil and onion.

This is breakfast after a morning in the woods near Spała.

Serves

2

Prep

5 min

Cook

10 min

Jump to the recipe

Ingredients

Mushrooms
  • 300g chanterelles, brushed clean
  • 1 small onion
  • 2 tbsp oil
To serve
  • 4 slices rye bread
  • Dill, salt, pepper

Method

1

Fry the mushrooms in a dry hot pan until their water cooks off.

2

Add the oil and chopped onion and fry until golden.

3

Pile onto toasted rye and cover with dill.

don't wash them

Notes from my kitchen

  • If you're not sure it's a chanterelle, take it to the sanepid inspector at the market. It's free.

Swaps that work

  • Any firm wild mushroom, or oyster mushrooms from a shop.

Keeping it

  • Eat it straight away.

posts.title: Notes from the market, September
posts.excerpt: Last cucumbers, first cabbages and the mushroom lady is back.
posts.content:
Saturday at Zielony Rynek, 8am. The cucumber crates are half the size they were a fortnight ago, which means pickling season is nearly over. The first white cabbages are in, huge and cheap.

The mushroom lady is back at her folding table by the tram stop. Chanterelles at 60 zł a kilo, ceps at 90. Cash only, as always.
